response.sql:
WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM Orders AS o
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25'
      AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44'
    GROUP BY c.gender
), average_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_order_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT gc.gender,
       gc.order_count,
       gc.order_count - ac.avg_order_count AS above_average
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac
WHERE gc.order_count > ac.avg_order_count;

assumptions.assumption: The average is across the per-gender counts for genders represented by at least one qualifying order; genders with no qualifying orders are not included.
